steps.note: Record what the legacy system does, per admitted entry point (verification/source-oracles/<slug>.json), compare the destination against it (compare-runtime-parity.py per entry point) and compose the receipt-bound summary (compose-parity-receipt.py). Expected values come only from the oracles; never from the card body, never from what the destination happens to return.
G-1..G-4 measured against the referent. Each evaluator writes its own verdict; a REFUSE here is a real outcome, not something to argue with.

The runner, fail-closed: snapshot the test reports before any rebuild, parse surefire, refuse a card body that pre-specifies a verdict, assert the tree is retrievable, run the pinned feeding gates so their receipts exist, then assert-pinned-gates-ran, assert-g4-claim-consistency and assert-no-fence-evasion. Feeding gates must run before the receipts are asserted or the floor refuses on an empty directory.

Author the verdict from the measured exit codes only, with an explicit failed_floors. A non-empty failed_floors makes the verdict REFUSE; checkers never author it and the card body never pre-specifies it.
Lint what was just written: the verdict against its schema, the floor receipts, and the claim tokens. This step can only agree or refuse; it cannot change the verdict.
